subject: lighthouse
pitch: A lighthouse on a tiny island.
reasoning:
I'm planning to build a lighthouse on a small island using mostly plain three.js primitives alongside the SDK's basic builder functions like joint and part, since I don't have full reference details for every helper signature.

I'm sketching the overall design: a dome-shaped island base with a tapered, banded lighthouse tower (alternating red/white cylinders), a gallery rail, glowing lantern room, conical roof, rocks, a small keeper's cottage, and an emissive warm-colored beam cone. I'm planning scale so the tower stands around 12m tall on a 6m-radius island, with the island's lowest edge touching the water plane at y=0.

Adding the gallery deck with a flattened torus railing, a lantern room with glass mullions, a conical red roof, and a finial sphere on top...

Now I'm sketching a small cottage box with a pyramid-style roof made from a low-segment cone, plus a brown door and dark windows. I'm scattering dodecahedron rocks around the island edge and considering a transparent yellow cone light beam extending outward from the lighthouse lantern.

I'm also setting up a helper function for building cylinder segments with varying top/bottom radii so I can taper the tower bands smoothly, then placing random rocks around the base with slight scale and position variation for a natural look.

Now I'm shaping the island itself: a sand hemisphere capped with a thin green grass disc, establishing where the tower base sits on top. Then I work out the tower's taper rate across its bands, plus the gallery disk and lantern room dimensions sitting at the very top.

Still placing details...

Working out the roof dimensions...

Working out the roof cone radius so the diagonal extent matches the base square, then settling on approximate values since the visual difference is negligible — time to just write the code and double-check variable names are defined.

I'm shaping the light beam as a tapered, rotated cylinder emanating from the lantern, using a translucent warm-colored material so it glows outward, then adding a simple circular water plane beneath for the sea, and naming the whole scene "lighthouse" before outputting the final code.
